root_cause.text: In arm64's ioremap_prot() path, a user-derived pgprot_t from generic_access_phys() was reused wholesale as a kernel I/O mapping, so user PTE permission bits such as PTE_USER were carried into the new mapping and made it inaccessible to the kernel under PAN.
root_cause.evidence: The commit/CVE states that generic_access_phys() passes a pgprot_t from the user mapping, that on arm64 this pgprot_t "contains all of the non-address bits from the pte, including the permission controls," and the patch fixes this by warning if the input is not a user mapping and rebuilding the mapping from PAGE_KERNEL while copying only PTE_ATTRINDX_MASK before calling __ioremap_prot().

vuln_statements.content: void __iomem *__ioremap_prot(phys_addr_t phys, size_t size, pgprot_t prot);

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In arm64's ioremap_prot() path, a user-derived pgprot_t from generic_access_phys() was reused wholesale as a kernel I/O mapping, so user PTE permission bits such as PTE_USER were carried into the new mapping and made it inaccessible to the kernel under PAN.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit/CVE states that generic_access_phys() passes a pgprot_t from the user mapping, that on arm64 this pgprot_t "contains all of the non-address bits from the pte, including the permission controls," and the patch fixes this by warning if the input is not a user mapping and rebuilding the mapping from PAGE_KERNEL while copying only PTE_ATTRINDX_MASK before calling __ioremap_prot().

intent_record.intent_summary: Make arm64 ioremap_prot derive safe kernel mappings from user pgprot memory attributes and reject invalid protections instead of passing raw pgprot values through.
intent_record.what: The patch replaces the direct macro alias '#define ioremap_prot __ioremap_prot' with a new static inline ioremap_prot() wrapper that extracts pgprot_val(user_prot), checks once with WARN_ON_ONCE that PTE_USER is set, returns NULL on failure, otherwise derives a kernel mapping protection by modifying PAGE_KERNEL with the user-supplied PTE_ATTRINDX_MASK bits and then calls __ioremap_prot(). It also removes the _PAGE_IOREMAP macro and adds an explicit ioremap(addr, size) macro that calls __ioremap_prot() with __pgprot(PROT_DEVICE_nGnRE).
intent_record.how: At runtime, ioremap_prot() no longer passes arbitrary caller-provided protections straight into __ioremap_prot(); instead it only accepts protections marked as user mappings, preserves only the memory attribute index from that input, and combines it with PAGE_KERNEL so the resulting ioremap uses kernel-safe permissions. Invalid callers now trigger a one-time warning and get NULL rather than creating a mapping with unsuitable attributes. The standard ioremap() path continues to create device nGnRE mappings explicitly.

grouping_result.intent: Make arm64 ioremap_prot derive safe kernel mappings from user pgprot memory attributes and reject invalid protections instead of passing raw pgprot values through.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause: it stops reusing raw user-derived pgprot values in arm64 ioremap_prot(), derives a safe kernel mapping from the memory attributes instead, and rejects invalid protections, preventing user-only bits like PTE_USER from being carried into kernel I/O mappings.

candidates.rationale: This macro aliases ioremap_prot directly to __ioremap_prot, allowing callers to pass a raw pgprot_t straight through into kernel I/O mapping creation. That direct pass-through is the root cause because user-derived permission bits like PTE_USER were reused unchanged.

candidates.content: void __iomem *__ioremap_prot(phys_addr_t phys, size_t size, pgprot_t prot);
candidates.rationale: This interface takes an arbitrary pgprot_t for kernel I/O remapping, embodying the unsafe design that reused caller-supplied protections wholesale instead of deriving safe kernel-only attributes.

vuln_statements.explanation: This alias made arm64 ioremap_prot directly invoke __ioremap_prot with the caller-supplied pgprot_t unchanged. That allowed user-derived permission bits such as PTE_USER from generic_access_phys() to be reused wholesale in a kernel I/O mapping, causing the PAN-related accessibility failure.

vuln_statements.stmt_text: void __iomem *__ioremap_prot(phys_addr_t phys, size_t size, pgprot_t prot);
vuln_statements.explanation: This interface exposed raw pgprot_t as the protection argument for kernel I/O remapping, enabling unsafe propagation of user PTE permission bits into kernel mappings instead of deriving sanitized kernel-only protections.
